Facts, relevant for disposal of this Rule, in brief, are that, Md Nozib Uddin alias Nazim had filed a Miscellaneous Case No. 27 of 2005, before the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Sujanagar, Pabna, against Md Mukul Mondal and 2 others under section 96(1) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act, 1950, seeking pre-emption in respect of the suit property. The claim of the petitioner's is that, he is co-sharer in the suit property comprising 0.073/4 acres of land lying at RS Plot Nos. 3526, 3527, 3528 and 3529 of Mouja Borojorpukuria, PS Sujanagar, District-Pabna, and further claimed that, the deed of exchange No.2769, dated 28-6-2005, on the basis of which the pre-emptee No.1 Mukul Mondol obtained title at suit property, is not in substance a sale deed and that the pre-emptor No.1 is a stranger of the suit property. 

 8. Learned Advocate Mr Mostafa Niaz Mahmood has appeared for the pre-emptee-appellant-opposite party No.1 and 3. He, on the other hand, submits that, the entire pleadings and the evidence on record, if considered together, then it will be evident the pre-emptor and the pre-emptee all are relatives and all are co-sharers in the suit property, but, this has not been disclosed in the application for pre-emption. He also submits that, the appellate court has rightly found that, the onus to prove that the deed of exchange No.2769, dated 28-6-2005 was a saf-kabala was upon the pre-emptor-petitioner and that he had failed to prove that, the deed of exchange was a deed of saf-kabala. He submits that, the burden to prove that the said sub-kabala deed was clearly rested on the pre-emptor-petitioner as per provisions of section 102 of the Evidence Act, 1872 as has been rightly held by the appellate court. As regards the boundary of the suit property, the learned Advocate also submits that, this has not been agitated before the court below. Moreover, in a pre-emption case the question of boundary is not the relevant issue, rather the relevant issue is as to whether the pre-emptor is a co-sharer in the suit property and whether the petition filed under section 96(1) of SAT Act, 1950, has merit and whether the petition was barred by limitation. The trial court has found that the suit was not barred by limitation and the appellate court has also concurred with this findings. Therefore, he submits that, the other issues need not be discussed here, because the transaction done by the deed of exchange No. 2669, dated 28-6-2005 was not a sale, rather it was a deed of exchange of property between pre-emptee No.1 and 2. Therefore, this petition filed under section 96 (1) of the SAT Act, 1950, was not competent. He concludes that, the Rule has no merit and the same is liable to be discharged.
